script: I helped him find the item, he exploded—my world turned upside down.. I was on the front desk when he walked in—six foot four, jacket all wrong, smell like cat urine or a gym locker room. He'd already been coming in every day for two weeks, staring at the shelves, then coming to me empty‑handed and asking, "How much is the red chair?" I'd have to ask, "Which chair?" and he'd get mad, like a kid who can't find his backpack. He'd never described the thing, so I couldn't just look up a price. Once, he actually brought the thing in a cardboard box, still sealed. I asked, "Can I see what's inside?" He rolled his eyes and said, "I didn't say what it was, I asked how much it was." I had to bring the supervisor over to explain, "You can't just close your eyes and ask a price." Today he was even more sullen. He came up and said, "How much is the clear tupperware?" I said, "Which ones?" He snapped, "NEVER ask 'which ones'!" and started yelling, "You asked me WHICH ONES?" My manager had to step in, tell him to bring the thing or leave. He bought the $2 pieces, and the manager took him outside, saying, "From now on, bring anything you want to talk about to the front or get out." He's not happy about that, and I think he's threatening to leave forever. I am not scared; I've got a squad of big guys ready to drag him out if he starts a fight. My manager's clear: if he doesn't act normal, he's not welcome back. That's the tea.
